2805058: Cupid Complaining to Venus is an oil painting by Lucas Cranach the Elder.
3235872: The Three Graces is an oil painting on beech panel of 1531 by Lucas Cranach the Elder. Other versions of the subject by the artist from 1530 and 1535 are in a private collection and the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City respectively.
3399390: The Portrait of Henry IV of Saxony and Catherine of Mecklenburg are a matching pair of full-length portrait paintings by the German Renaissance master Lucas Cranach the Elder, dating from 1514, now in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden, Germany.
Portraits of Henry IV of Saxony and Catherine of Mecklenburg
3605055: Adam and Eve is a pair of paintings by German Renaissance master Lucas Cranach the Elder, dating from 1528, housed in the Uffizi, Florence, Italy.
3842524: Madonna with Child with Young John the Baptist is a painting by the German Renaissance painter Lucas Cranach the Elder, dating from 1514. It is housed in the Uffizi Gallery of Florence.
Madonna with Child with Young John the Baptist (Cranach)
3937781: The Female Portrait is a painting by German Renaissance master Lucas Cranach the Elder, dating from around 1530, now housed in the Uffizi Gallery of Florence, Italy.
4289290: Melancholia is an oil-on-panel painting by the German painter Lucas Cranach the Elder, created in 1532. It is held in the National Gallery of Denmark in Copenhagen.
5676406: Cardinal Albert of Brandenburg before Christ on the Cross is a painting by Lucas Cranach the Elder. It is dated 1520–1530.
Cardinal Albert of Brandenburg before Christ on the Cross
7728256: Crucifixion is an oil painting by German artist Lucas Cranach the Elder. One of many versions of the subject painted by Cranach, this one, created in 1532, is now in the Indianapolis Museum of Art.
9191516: Christ Blessing the Children is a religious oil painting created by the German Renaissance artist Lucas Cranach the Elder and his workshop in 1537.
Christ Blessing the Children (Lucas Cranach the Elder)
18599401: The Ill-Matched Couple is a 1532 oil painting by the German Renaissance painter Lucas Cranach the Elder. It was owned by Maximilian I of Bavaria until 1632, when Swedish troops captured it in a raid on Munich and thus is now in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
19901683: The Madonna and Child is a painting by Lucas Kranach the Elder (1472–1553). The oil painting was probably brought to Poland by Jan Sulimirski and placed in the parish church of Sulimierzyce, the ancestral seat of the Sulimirski/Sulimierski family around 1550.
19911426: The Martyrdom of Saint Barbara is an early 16th century painting by German artist Lucas Cranach the Elder. It is in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, in New York.
The Martyrdom of Saint Barbara (Lucas Cranach the Elder)
19911452: The Judgment of Paris is a 1528 painting by the German artist Lucas Cranach the Elder. It depicts the myth of Paris, Prince of Troy, selecting the fairest goddess from among Minerva, Juno, and Venus.
19911613: Saint Maurice is a painting attributed to Lucas Cranach the Elder and his workshop depicting Saint Maurice, an early Christian martyr from North Africa. It was made for a church in Halle (Saale), specifically Marktkirche, as the interior left wing of a larger paneled altarpiece.
Saint Maurice (Lucas Cranach the Elder and Workshop)
19911797: Lukas Spielhausen is a 16th-century portrait by German artist Lucas Cranach the Elder. Done in oil and gold on beechwood, the painting is in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.
20729896: Adam and Eve is a c. 1538 oil on limewood painting by Lucas Cranach the Elder, acquired in 1949 from the Cistercian monastery in Osek near Duchcov, now in the National Gallery Prague.
20828882: The Fountain of Youth is an oil-on-panel painting executed in 1546 by the German artist Lucas Cranach the Elder. It depicts a version of the Fountain of Youth.
21614134: Caritas is an oil on panel painting by German painter Lucas Cranach the Elder. The painting is kept in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts, Antwerp.
24930037: Portrait of a Saxon Noblewoman is an oil on canvas painting by Lucas Cranach the Elder. It has been in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon since 1892.
26197830: Law and Grace is considered one of the most important paintings by Lucas Cranach the Elder.
26215807: The Prague Altarpiece of Lucas Cranach the Elder portrays the Virgin Mary and female saints was, at the time it was made, the second most important altarpiece in St Vitus Cathedral.
Prague Altarpiece of Lucas Cranach the Elder
30302632: Wittenberg Cranach Altarpiece is one of the major Lutheran winged altarpieces created by Lucas Cranach the Elder and his son Lucas Cranach the Younger for the Evangelical Lutheran City and Parish Church of St. Mary's in Wittenberg, Germany.
46473788: The Adoration of the Shepherds is a c. 1515–1520 oil on panel painting of the Nativity by the German artist Lucas Cranach the Elder in the collection of the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister in Dresden.
Adoration of the Shepherds (Lucas Cranach the Elder)
52254163: Law and Grace is considered one of the most important paintings by Lucas Cranach the Elder. As the second one of the early versions of the work, it is also known as ‘the Gotha type’ - the other is 'the Prague type'.
56648748: Melancholia is a 1532 oil painting by the German artist Lucas Cranach the Elder. It is now in the Unterlinden Museum in Colmar, France.
64787019: The Torgauer Altar, Torgau Altarpiece or Altarpiece of the Holy Kinship is a triptych altarpiece painted by Lucas Cranach the Elder in 1509.
68009759: Adam and Eve is a c. 1508–1510 oil on limewood panel by Lucas Cranach the Elder, now in the Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon. It is one of the earliest in a series of works by the artist showing the fall of man, also including examples now in Florence and in Prague.
83383248: The Procuress is an oil-on-panel painting by the German Renaissance painter Lucas Cranach the Elder, created in 1548. The style of the painting is the Northern Renaissance.
96678699: Lamentation over the Dead Body of Christ is an oil painting on wood panel completed by a follower of the German Renaissance artist Lucas Cranach the Elder during the 1530s. It is considered to be among the most valued works of art to have been plundered from Polish collections during World War II.
Lamentation (School of Lucas Cranach the Elder)
107438601: Albert of Brandenburg as Saint Jerome is a 1527 oil on panel painting by Lucas Cranach the Elder, who was a Protestant but also worked for Catholic patrons. It shows Albert of Brandenburg.
Albert of Brandenburg as Saint Jerome
113375854: The Schneeberg Altarpiece is a Lutheran winged altarpiece created in 1539 by Lucas Cranach the Elder for the Church of St. Wolfgang in Schneeberg in Saxony, Germany.
115826047: Venus and Cupid with a Honeycomb is an oil painting by the German artist Lucas Cranach the Elder, one of the masters of the German Renaissance. It was probably executed in 1531 after Cranach met Georg Sabinus, a German poet, diplomat and academic at the University of Wittenberg.
Venus and Cupid with a Honeycomb
117071454: Weimar Cranach Altarpiece is a Lutheran winged altarpiece created by Lucas Cranach the Elder and his son Lucas Cranach the Younger between 1552 and 1555 for the Church of St. Peter und Paul in Weimar, Germany.
120605163: The Spring Nymph at the Fountain is the earliest example of a series of paintings by Renaissance artists Lucas Cranach the Elder and Lucas Cranach the Younger, depicting a resting spring nymph. There are at least 24 versions that were made in the Cranach workshop in Wittenberg.

131295397: Adam and Eve is a 1533 oil on panel painting by Lucas Cranach the Elder, dated on the rock at the bottom by Adam. It is now in the Museum der bildenden Künste in Leipzig, to which it was donated by the Sternburg Foundation.
133444154: Law and Gospel is one of a number of thematically linked, allegorical panel paintings by Lucas Cranach the Elder from about 1529. The paintings, intended to illustrate Lutheran ideas of salvation, are exemplars of Lutheran Merkbilder, which were simple, didactic illustrations of Christian doctrine.
